tagline.text: Red-brick Holy Cross church in Nabua, Camarines Sur, founded in 1578

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season (including the May 3 feast day)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~900 (round-trip transport from Naga included, per person for a day trip)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Naga Airport (WNP) or Bicol International Airport (DRP)

children.text: Nabua Church is formally the Holy Cross Parish. It grew out of a church founded by Franciscan missionaries in 1578, and the present building was completed in 1700. A red-brick facade, a bell tower and a 1939 historical marker remain, and the Boa-Boahan Festival is held every year on the May 3 feast day.

Nabua Church is a Roman Catholic church in the very center of Nabua, Camarines Sur, under the Archdiocese of Caceres. Its formal name is Holy Cross Parish Church. Some write-ups give a different patron saint, but Wikipedia and the parish information we checked all name the Holy Cross. When asking for directions, simply say
Nabua Church
or Holy Cross.

Its history goes back to 1578. The Franciscan friars Pablo de Jesus and Bartolome Ruiz preached in the area and founded a church, and several surrounding settlements are said to have been united around it. The old name of the place was Lupa, and village names such as Antacodos, Sabang and Binoyoan appear alongside it. The first building burned in 1610, the second, built in 1611, was destroyed by a typhoon, and a third church was built between 1630 and 1656. The church standing today was completed in 1700.

Hardship did not end there. According to the historical marker, an earthquake damaged the bell tower in 1850 and it was repaired around 1890–1894, and a typhoon unroofed the church in 1875 and it was repaired in 1878. In 1939 the Philippine Historical Committee declared it a heritage church and placed a historical marker on the facade. The best story here is a building that has endured earthquakes, typhoons and floods for more than 400 years and has watched over the town.

In appearance it is a plain red-brick building rather than a flamboyant Baroque church. The front wall has large pilasters topped with finials, and arched windows flank the main portal and run across the upper wall. The bell tower is attached on the right side (the epistle side). If you have already seen the big churches of Naga, a quiet small town where you can take in the church and everyday local life together offers a different flavor. Nabua is called the mother town of nearby towns such as Iriga, Buhi, Bato, Balatan, Bula and Baao, and the speech that became the base of Rinconada Bikol, the Bikol language of this area, came from here. It helps to see the church as a building at the center of that regional history.

The deep-red brick facade rises up to four levels. Large pilasters, finials above them and regular arched windows make it easy to spot from a distance. The brick looks richest early in the morning or as the sun gets low.

A historical marker installed in 1939 stands on the facade. It sums up the church's chronology: founded in 1578, burned in 1610, hit by a typhoon in 1611, completed in 1700, the 1850 earthquake, and the 1875 typhoon with repairs in 1878. It is worth keeping a photo of it.

The bell tower is attached to the right side of the church. It was damaged by the 1850 earthquake and rebuilt, and in this earthquake-prone region it has been repaired several times. Some people say the tower looks tilted, but we could not find any confirmed source, so judge for yourself when you see it. Just looking up from the base gives a sense of the thickness of a structure that has survived earthquakes and typhoons for so long.

One visitor account describes an entrance with the Latin words Porta Sancta (Holy Door) in stainless steel, an angel at the center and statues of Saint Peter and Saint Paul on either side. The metal doors show Jesus embracing someone. Its appearance may change during construction or events.

The interior retablo shows delicate carvings of vines and flowers and a Patriarchal cross at the center. During Mass or on wedding days you cannot get close, so view it quietly from the back or choose a time with no events.

Some of the stained-glass windows are said to show local stories, such as the arrival of Christianity with Mayon Volcano in the background. They are worth a slow look, where religious art meets the local landscape.
Outside the church there is a shrine to the Virgin Mary and a statue of Nuestra Señora Angustia. A local legend says that an apparition of Angustia saved the town from an earthquake and a flood.

On the May 3 feast of the Holy Cross, the area holds the Boa-Boahan Festival. It revives an old "Boa feast" connected with coconut embryos (boa), and the first festival was held in 1975. Crowds gather then, so plan your schedule and lodging ahead of time.

items.title: Day trip from Naga
items.subtitle: The church and a loop through town

children.text: Take a bus or van toward Nabua from a terminal in Naga. Check the boarding point and times locally. The distance is about
37km
and by car it usually takes about
40 minutes–1 hour
Arrive in Nabua town and start with the church facade. The red brick looks its best in the morning light. Read the 1939 historical marker on the front and photograph it.
Look up slowly at the bell tower and the facade, then, if there is no Mass or event, go inside to see the retablo and the stained-glass windows. Dress modestly.
See the Marian shrine and the Angustia statue outside the church, then stroll the streets of the town around it.
Have lunch at a restaurant in town. Bicol food often uses coconut milk and chili, so ask about the spice level first.
Head back toward Naga. Be sure to check the last departure time locally.

Bus and van times change often. It is safer to check your return transport as soon as you arrive. The church is not large, so an hour or two is enough even at a slow pace, and the rest of the time suits sightseeing in town or a meal.
First visit Naga Metropolitan Cathedral and the churches in the city.
Have lunch in Naga and rest. In the evening, walk around your lodging.
Travel to Nabua and see the church and the town.
Continue toward Iriga, or head straight back to Naga. Iriga is the neighboring city that borders Nabua on the east.
During festival periods, check lodging and transport ahead of time.
From Manila to Nabua it is about
470km
by road. Long-distance buses from Manila toward Naga or Iriga are the usual choice, and travel time varies greatly with traffic.

Flights between Manila and Naga (Naga Airport, WNP, in Pili) change with the season, so check the airline's latest schedule. You can also fly to Bicol International Airport (DRP) and continue by road.
Check the latest notices from bus companies and airlines for exact timetables and fares.
Nabua is about
37km
from Naga. Travel sites list a direct bus from Naga to Nabua (for example Peñafrancia Tours and Travel), and the number of daily trips differs from source to source.
By rental car or taxi it usually takes around
30–40 minutes
. By bus or van, including transfers, it can take
about 1 hour or more
The church is in the center of Nabua. Within town you can get around by tricycle or on foot. Ask the driver for the fare and agree on it before you ride.
For the church alone, the dry season with less rain is more comfortable. Still, March to May is very hot at midday, so it is better to go in the morning.

The feast of the Holy Cross on May 3 brings the Boa-Boahan Festival and the most energy. In return, crowds gather and transport and lodging get tight. The rainy and typhoon season from June to November can disrupt plans, and after Typhoon Usman in 2018 there was flooding around Nabua.

Nabua is not a destination with a wide range of lodging. Most people visit as a day trip, and if you need to stay overnight, using Naga as a base gives you more choices. Book early during festival periods. Nabua had about 86,000 people in the 2024 census and is made up of 42 barangays, so rural scenery continues once you leave the town center.

In town restaurants you can try traditional Bicol dishes made with coconut milk and chili. We could not confirm any famous restaurants, so ask locals for recommendations. It is a good idea to check hygiene and prices before you order.
Entering during Mass is difficult, so check the times before you go. For one sample week, weekdays were listed at
in the morning and
in the evening, with several Masses on Sunday and some in English. Times can change from week to week, so ask the parish office.
Dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered.
On wedding or event days the parking lot fills up and photographing the interior is difficult. It helps to check the schedule in advance.
Ask permission and take interior photos quietly. Refrain from photography during Mass.
The parish phone number is listed as (054) 288 3762. You can call before your visit to ask about opening hours.
For a day trip, check the return transport times as soon as you arrive.
The church is in the center of town, so it is easy to walk around the area. At midday the sun is strong, though, so bring a hat and water.
Nabua has local customs such as Lenten processions, All Saints events and serenades. If the timing fits, check for event notices in and around the church.

The church name differs between sources. The sources we checked call it the Holy Cross church, and locally it is fine to call it Nabua Church. In typhoon season, leave plenty of room in your schedule.
Some sources give a different patron saint and feast day. Several sources confirm the May 3 feast of the Holy Cross.
Bus and van times and fares change often, so check locally.
Festivals and Mass times are crowded, so keep a close eye on your belongings.
The church is a place of worship, so avoid noise and large camera equipment during Mass.
Typhoons and heavy rain can block roads or cause flooding, so check the weather forecast.
The cathedral in Naga is about
37km
from Nabua. Using Naga as a base makes it easy to visit both together.
The hub city of the Bicol region, with plenty of lodging and restaurants. Transport to Nabua also leaves from here.
The largest religious festival in the Bicol region, held in Naga in September. If the timing works, add it to your itinerary.
A neighboring city bordering Nabua on the east. The travel distance is short, but check attractions and transport locally.
